claim: Several states, Oregon among them, hold their producers to a stricter figure.
because: The question is about a Cabernet Sauvignon label. Oregon's stricter rule is 90 percent, but OAR 845-010-0915 lists Cabernet Sauvignon among the grapes that may still be labelled at 75 percent. The others on that list are Cabernet Franc, Carmenère, Durif, Grenache, Malbec, Marsanne, Merlot, Mourvèdre, Petit Verdot, Roussanne, Sangiovese, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Syrah, Tannat, Tempranillo and Zinfandel. So an Oregon Cabernet has the same 75 percent floor as the federal rule. As written, the explanation teaches that it needs more.
fix: Federal law sets the varietal floor at 75 percent, so a quarter of the blend can be something else entirely. Some states go further: Oregon asks 90 percent for most varieties, though Cabernet Sauvignon is one of the grapes it still allows at 75.
